summary: Streaming reconnect resumes on prewarm session and overrides explicit tenant model pin, causing fallback to canary variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightChat has an explicit tenant-level model pin to redwood/open-7b-v2-quant for an SLA-sensitive route. During a streaming reconnect (client retried after a transient 502), the resumed stream was attached to an existing prewarm session owned by a canary cohort. The routing layer applied the prewarm session's metadata and routed the resumed request to the canary variant instead of honoring the tenant pin.

Impact:
- BrightChat observed degraded quality responses for ~6 minutes for ~1200 requests (partial sessions) while their tenant pin was effectively bypassed.
- Cost spike: routed to a larger variant intermittently causing token billing increase.
- Customer-facing latency and content regressions; they opened an incident citing production impact.

Environment:
- Production, us-east cluster (region: us-east-1).
- Dedicated capacity pool id: ded-nyc-3 (BrightChat).
- Canary rollout active for redwood/open-7b-v2-quant: weight 7%.

Steps to reproduce (from customer):
1) Configure tenant TID-992 with explicit model_pin=redwood/open-7b-v2-quant via Console.
2) Trigger a streaming generation that prewarms canary pods (small warmup traffic).
3) Cause a transient 502 on the edge for the client and have the client reconnect the same stream id.
4) Observe routing decision in logs and confirm model id selected.

Observed behavior:
- Resumed stream was routed to canary variant (redwood/open-7b-v2-quant-canary-2026-02-09) despite tenant model_pin setting.
- Edge trace id: trace-us-east-0a-8f7c9b2d.
- Orchestrator decision log snippet: "selected_session=prewarm-session-cc33, effective_model=canary-variant, tenant_pin_present=true"

Expected behavior:
- Tenant model_pin must override ephemeral prewarm-session attachments; resumed streams should respect the tenant-level pin and route to the pinned variant or fallback according to explicit routing policy.

Logs & artifacts attached (provided by customer and support):
- Edge traces: trace-us-east-0a-8f7c9b2d, trace-us-east-0a-8f7c9b3f.
- Orchestrator decision dump (sanitized): decision-2026-02-10-14-22.log (attached).
- Customer sample prompts + responses showing quality delta (attached).
comments: Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-02-10: Filed on behalf of BrightChat. Attached edge traces and decision logs. Customer reports immediate quality regression and cost bump. Requesting SRE triage and a short-term mitigation to prevent further user impact.

SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-02-10: Acknowledged. Reproduced locally using a simulated streaming reconnect. Initial hypothesis: routing priority comparator incorrectly ranks active prewarm session metadata above tenant pin when both are present on a resumed stream. Collecting more traces and adding debug logging in routing-mesh decision path.

Customer (BrightChat, Elena Rivera) 2026-02-10: Impact confirmed. We can temporarily stop canary traffic but prefer a hotfix to ensure pins are authoritative. Provided request IDs and session ids on our side.

SRE (Diego Morales) 2026-02-11: Found comparator behavior in routing-mesh: prewarm sessions set session_priority='session' while tenant pins set session_priority='pin' but comparator logic treats non-empty strings with lexical precedence so 'session' > 'pin' in current implementation. Posting proposed fix to override comparator to check explicit_pin boolean first. Preparing PR and test cases.

Support (Aisha Patel) 2026-02-11: Communicated workaround to BrightChat: (1) disable canary weight for the impacted model in us-east, (2) create a CLI-level model override for tenant route via route.override_model_id until the patch is deployed. Customer applied workaround and reports traffic reverted to pinned model; monitoring continues.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings:
- Reproducible: yes, with streaming reconnect flow.
- Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by log inspection): priority comparator in routing-mesh used lexicographic ordering on a small set of session_priority tokens rather than explicit flag semantics. Because 'session' sorts after 'pin', prewarm session metadata won when both present.
- Secondary contributing factor: resumed streams reattach session metadata before pin reconciliation runs, so the mid-path comparator had to disambiguate and it currently doesn't check explicit_pin boolean early.
- Risk: any resumed streaming clients that reconnect to a prewarm session may temporarily bypass tenant pins during a rollout window.
- Test coverage gap: no unit test validated session vs pin precedence with streaming reconnect semantics.

Next steps:
- Create PR to change comparator to: if explicit_pin present => choose pin; else consider session metadata. Add unit tests for streaming-reconnect scenarios. (PR opened in routing-mesh repo).
- Backfill a small reconciler job to find tenants whose live sessions are attached to prewarm canary pods and reassign or evict sessions if tenant_pin exists. This mitigates already-affected customers until roll-out of fix.
- Post-deploy: run a Canary simulation harness for streaming reconnect permutations.
workaround: Applied by customer: temporarily set canary weight for redwood/open-7b-v2-quant in us-east to 0% and created a route.override_model_id for tenant TID-992. Support recommended restarting affected prewarm sessions (or blocking reuse) as a short-term mitigation. This restored pinned routing and prevented further regressions.
resolution: Fix in progress: routing-mesh comparator patch authored and under review. Reconciler plan drafted for immediate remediation. Target patch deployment to prod us-east: 2026-02-12 (pending review and QA).
follow_up_actions: PR review and merge: routing-mesh comparator fix (https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing-mesh/pull/891)
Deploy reconciler job to us-east to evict/rewire prewarm sessions that conflict with explicit tenant pins
Add unit/integration tests covering streaming reconnect + pin precedence
Communicate root cause and postmortem to BrightChat when incident closed
